property_summary: Only the contract owner can change the owner; after attempting changeOwner by caller X, owner() remains unchanged unless X was the original owner.
After calling changeOwner(x) as the current owner, owner() equals the externally provided newOwner argument.
Calling changeOwner(newOwner) while msg.sender is the current owner results in owner() equal to msg.sender (the caller), i.e. ownership becomes the caller, not tx.origin or the provided newOwner.

When the current owner calls changeOwner(newOwner), the contract's owner() becomes equal to the provided newOwner (i.e., ownership is set from the parameter), not some other external caller like tx.origin.
When the current owner invokes changeOwner(newOwner), the contract's owner() becomes equal to the externally supplied newOwner argument (i.e. owner is set from the function parameter).

After any external call (here allowance) made by an EOA caller, the contract's owner() must equal msg.sender (the immediate caller) when changeOwner is invoked by that same msg.sender as owner — i.e., owner cannot be changed to tx.origin through an intermediate external call by the owner.

Calling allowance(a,b) is a view that must not change contract owner; the mutant sets owner to tx.origin in changeOwner and thus can produce a differing _owner after allowance-related interactions where only the original contract's owner should be controllable (the reference never changes owner via an unrelated call).

Calling allowance(...) must never change the contract owner; the buggy mutant that assigns _owner = tx.origin in changeOwner can be made to change owner via an external call path where tx.origin differs (the reference never changes owner through such an allowance-driven interaction).

Calling the view function allowance(address,uint256) must never change the contract owner; the mutant that sets _owner = tx.origin in changeOwner can be made to change owner via an external call path where tx.origin differs, so the reference keeps owner unchanged for all inputs while the mutant can produce a differing owner for some inputs.

Calling the view function allowance(address owner, address spender) does not change contract ownership in the reference implementation for any inputs, but the mutant (which sets _owner = tx.origin inside changeOwner) can cause _owner to differ after such an interaction when an external call path triggers changeOwner with tx.origin controlled, so the property is violated for some inputs.
